d.g: Of or pertaining to a wife, or her genes or relatives.

d.x: Riccabocca, the wiliest and most relentless of men in his maxims, melted into absolute uxorial imbecility at the sight of that mute distress.

uxorial.e: From Latin uxōrius (“of or pertaining to a wife; overly fond of one’s wife”) + English -al (suffix forming adjectives). Uxōrius is derived from uxor (“wife”) + -ius (suffix forming adjectives).

d.g: Very devoted and possibly submissive to one's wife; showing excessive uxorial devotion.
d.x: In truth, Richard was a fond—almost an uxorious husband.

uxorious.e: Borrowed from Latin uxōrius (“of or pertaining to a wife”), from uxor (“wife”) + -ious.

d.g: (legal terminology) the Latin word for wife
The murdering of one's own wife.

uxoricide.e: From French uxoricide or Latin uxor + English -icide.

d.g: Overt devotion or submissiveness to one's wife.
d.x: The uxoriousness of Charles [the First] is re-echoed by all the writers of a certain party.

d.g: An inordinate fear of one's own wife, or of wives.
Overt devotion or submissiveness to one's wife.

d.x: Dicky […] made his best pace to a recess in a back street, there to examine his pogues; for though the uxter was gone from them, they might yet bring a few coppers from Mr Weech, if they were of good quality.
